rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a blastocyst assessment and appropriately caveated, but it overstates confidence in visible ICM/TE quality from this single somewhat collapsed image and repeats the provided 3AA label rather than strictly image-based morphology.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, male factor, endometrium, cycle history, and cohort size with embryo quality and overall prognosis.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with prognosis appropriately tied to embryo quality and patient age; only minor overinterpretation of morphology and cohort-size implications.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice guidelines: SET in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst, no routine PGT-A at age 28, and cautious interpretation after one failed transfer. Minor issue: some counseling points are more pragmatic than guideline-based.
Provides clear next-step recommendations for transfer management, luteal support considerations, lifestyle advice, and contingency planning for future cycles with appropriate nuance.
